parts.label: Understand
parts.title: Name the value before the pilot
parts.body:
An AI project may pass a model test and still leave the business worse off. Start with the decision the organization hopes to improve and the population of work it affects. Record the current outcome, the expected mechanism of improvement, the cost of making the change, and a measure that would reveal damage. For a claims assistant, a useful outcome might be the cost per correctly resolved claim with no increase in reopened cases. Prompt volume and employee enthusiasm tell you something about use, but neither establishes that outcome.

Separate three claims that are often blended together. A model can perform a task on an evaluation set; staff can adopt it in a live workflow; and the organization can realize a financial or service benefit. Evidence for one does not establish the others. Before approving a pilot, write the baseline period, eligible cases, quality standard, and date when a scale decision will be made. If the workflow is seasonal, compare like periods or record the difference in case mix.

Released time needs an explicit destination. Ten minutes saved on each case may increase capacity or shorten queues. It reduces cash spending only if staffing, overtime, or external spend actually falls. Finance and the business owner should agree how each form of value will be reported, with double counting removed.

example.title: From speed to a defensible outcome
example.body: An illustrative team handles 6,000 eligible cases each month. A pilot cuts average preparation time from 20 to 14 minutes, but review adds two minutes and the reopen rate rises from 4% to 5%. Report four net minutes of capacity per case and the quality concern. Do not call the full six minutes a payroll saving. The business owner must decide whether the extra rework is acceptable before expansion.

exercise.title: Write a value hypothesis
exercise.body: Choose one AI use case. State its eligible population, baseline period, primary outcome with unit, quality countermeasure, cost owner, and the operational change that would convert time released into value. Ask a finance partner which claimed benefit would appear in a budget and which would remain capacity or service value.

sources: NIST AI RMF Core: context, measurement, and management
OECD: adoption of AI in firms and organizational barriers

parts.label: Practice
parts.title: Design a credible comparison
parts.body:
A before-and-after chart can mislead when demand, staffing, or case difficulty changes. A practical pilot compares similar eligible work handled at the same time, with assignment rules set before the trial. Random assignment is useful when feasible. Otherwise match teams or case types, document the differences, and keep the claim appropriately modest. Record the share of eligible cases actually using the tool. A result for expert volunteers may not transfer to everyone expected to use it.

Agree how to count exceptions before results arrive. Failed generations, manual overrides, escalations, and cases withdrawn from the pilot belong in the denominator if the scaled workflow would face them. Measure the entire path to a resolved outcome, including human checking and downstream corrections. Review samples for errors that averages conceal, especially in work affecting customers, employees, or access to services. NIST calls for documented measurement and monitoring that continues after deployment.

Present an observed effect with its uncertainty and limits. A small sample of routine cases can support continued testing, but is weak evidence for a national rollout involving rare, high impact cases. The executive decision is often to expand the test population, narrow the intended use, or add safeguards.

example.title: Two service queues
example.body: Suppose two comparable queues each receive 1,000 eligible tickets. The assisted queue resolves 850 within the service target and reopens 65; the comparison queue resolves 820 and reopens 40. The service target improved by three percentage points while reopens worsened by 2.5 points. Examine ticket mix and reopen causes before assigning a monetary benefit.

exercise.title: Plan a pilot comparison
exercise.body: Specify which cases qualify, how they will be assigned, the comparison, a minimum observation period, and how you will count non-use, corrections, and failed requests. Name one plausible confounder and the evidence you will collect to check it.

sources: NIST AI RMF Playbook: measure and production comparison
NIST AI RMF Core: Measure 2.4 and Manage 4.1

parts.label: Operate
parts.title: Build a benefits ledger
parts.body:
A portfolio slide often adds incompatible numbers: employee hours, avoided losses, new revenue, and forecast opportunity. Maintain a benefits ledger that records each use case's baseline, counterfactual, observed outcome, cost, confidence, owner, and period. Give realized and forecast benefits separate columns. Record whether an outcome is cash, released capacity, service quality, risk reduction, or a strategic option. Do not sum the categories as if they were all cash.

The ledger should identify overlap. If a sales assistant and a pricing model both claim the same increase in conversion, the business owner must assign or apportion the benefit. If an assistant reduces handling time, the unit economics calculation should include review and rework. For risk reduction, report an exposure measure and assumptions rather than pretending an incident that did not happen has a precise avoided dollar value. Finance can validate cash effects; operations can validate capacity; the risk owner can validate exposure changes.

Use a monthly review to update decisions: continue, improve, expand, pause, or retire. Include changes in input mix, user behavior, model performance, and vendor charges. A pilot result loses force if the deployed system serves different users or costs far more at the intended scale. The ledger needs dates, owners, and a next decision.

example.title: An honest portfolio line
example.body: Illustrative claim: 240 analyst hours released in a month, 90 hours redeployed to backlog clearance, no staffing reduction, and a 1.2 percentage point increase in corrections. The ledger records capacity and a quality countermeasure. It does not add the full 240 hours to cash savings and then add the backlog improvement again.

exercise.title: Reconcile two claims
exercise.body: Draft ledger entries for two tools that both affect the same customer workflow. Identify a shared outcome, assign an owner for attribution, and write what evidence would allow finance to recognize a cash benefit. Keep a separate line for service or capacity gains.

sources: NIST AI RMF Core: ongoing monitoring and risk response

parts.label: Apply
parts.title: Make the scale recommendation
parts.body:
An investment recommendation should fit on one page before its supporting analysis. State the use case and affected population; the observed outcome against its comparison; quality and risk measures; total cost; uncertainties; and the decision requested. Explain how the outcome will hold up when users, languages, regions, or case types change. Set a next review date and a stop condition. If the evidence is mixed, say so plainly.

Suppose a Canadian and EU service organization pilots one English language workflow. The pilot may support further testing, but it does not establish performance for French language service, other member states, or cases governed by different obligations. Budget for evaluation and local expertise before a cross-region launch. This is an application of disciplined generalization, not a claim that every use case is regulated in the same way.

The CAIO should recommend a choice the executive can accept or reject: expand under stated limits, fund another test, redesign, or stop. Attach the business owner and the person with authority to accept residual risk. Record what evidence would change the recommendation. This turns a measurement report into an investment decision.

example.title: A bounded approval
example.body: Approve a 12-week expansion from one queue to three, capped at an illustrative $180,000 including review labor. Require no deterioration in the reopen rate, a measured reduction in cost per correctly resolved case, and evaluation of French cases before a bilingual rollout. These are invented decision terms for the exercise, not general benchmarks.

exercise.title: Write the decision memo
exercise.body: Using your pilot plan, write a 150-word recommendation with observed benefit, one countermeasure, total incremental cost, limits of the comparison, scale boundary, stop rule, and named approver. Ask a peer to challenge the weakest assumption.

sources: NIST AI RMF Core: contextual mapping and monitored deployment
